content.title: Men’s NCAA Tournament power rankings: Which Sweet 16 teams look championship-worthy?
content.text: Editor’s note: This article is part of the Bracket Central series, an inside look at the run-up to the men’s & women’s NCAA Tournaments, along with analysis and picks during the tournaments.The lack of upsets over the first two days of the NCAA Tournament was a major storyline heading into the second round. High Point was the only team seeded No. 12 or higher to win a first-round game, but the flip side of the lack of upsets was that the weekend brought some phenomenal matchups.Many of those high-level clashes delivered, highlighted by the Kansas-St. John’s thriller in San Diego. Bill Self and Rick Pitino went back and forth in a tremendous chess match that ended with a buzzer-beater from an unlikely hero, Red Storm point guard Dylan Darling. Mere hours later, Florida, the reigning national champs, became the first No. 1 seed to fall thanks to a stunning upset by Iowa. That result ensured the Final Four will not be all top seeds for the second straight year and busted the South Region wide open, though No. 2 seed Houston will be the clear favorite now, playing the next two rounds in its home city.Your browser does not support the video tag.Another massive storyline: the dominance of the Big Ten. Six of the league’s nine NCAA Tournament qualifiers made the Sweet 16, one shy of the record set by the SEC last year, and only two representatives lost their first game (Wisconsin and Ohio State). The league had impressive depth all season long, and it has a real chance to end its 26-year national championship drought.Arizona could not fully escape Utah State, but the Wildcats did ultimately win by 12 and are on to their third consecutive Sweet 16. Jaden Bradley (18 points), Brayden Burries (16 points, nine rebounds) and Motiejus Krivas (11 points, 14 rebounds) were all terrific in the victory. Tommy Lloyd has yet to make it past the Sweet 16 as a head coach, and to do it this year he’ll have to get past John Calipari and Arkansas on Thursday in San Jose. The point guard battle between Bradley and freshman phenom Darius Acuff should be a classic. Saint Louis hit some shots in the first half to keep things close, but Michigan overwhelmed the Billikens in the final 20 minutes en route to a comfortable 23-point victory. Yaxel Lendeborg’s 25 points and Michigan’s collection of thunderous dunks were simply too much for the No. 9 seed to handle. The Wolverines have a wide-open path to the Final Four: Their Sweet 16 opponent, Alabama, is still without second-leading scorer Aden Holloway, and the Midwest Region’s No. 2 seed, Iowa State, lost star forward Joshua Jefferson to a bad ankle injury.After an incredibly shaky opening performance against Siena, Duke played a dazzling second half against TCU on Saturday, leaning on elite defense to hold off the Horned Frogs. Cameron Boozer was his typical exceptional self (19 points, 11 rebounds, four assists, three steals), and Duke also got 13 minutes out of Patrick Ngongba II, who had missed the previous five games with a foot injury. With Ngongba back in the fold and another few days to rest, the Blue Devils vault back up into the top three of these rankings.Zero drama for Houston in getting to the Sweet 16 this year. The Cougars won both of their opening-weekend games by 31 points, impressively dispatching Texas A&M in the second round. The scary part: Houston did not even shoot it well in that game, going just 8 of 31 (25.8%) from deep, but it still tallied 1.34 points per possession. Kelvin Sampson’s team will be tested in the paint by Illinois’ gigantic frontcourt, led by the Ivisic twins, but the Cougars do have the advantage of the game being played in Houston.The Boilermakers got past Miami (Fla.) on Sunday largely on the strength of their four-year trio of Braden Smith, Fletcher Loyer and Trey Kaufman-Renn. That group combined for 55 points, and each player logged at least 35 minutes. Purdue’s path to the Final Four caught a break with No. 3 seed Gonzaga going down against Texas, setting up a matchup with the No. 11 seed in San Jose. One concern is that starting guard CJ Cox left Sunday’s win with a hyperextended knee, though he said after the game that he expected to be ready to go in the Sweet 16.Illinois coasted into the Sweet 16, winning its first two games by a combined 56 points. Every member of the Illini’s eight-man rotation has made significant contributions so far, giving Brad Underwood balance beyond star guard Keaton Wagler. Defense was viewed as Illinois’ Achilles’ heel, but it held VCU to just 0.83 points per possession on Saturday. If the Illini can buckle down on that end, their explosive offense could get them to a Final Four. They will have to beat Houston in Houston on Thursday to get there, though.The Huskies defeated UCLA in the battle of the combustible coaches, getting a huge game from Alex Karaban (27 points) and an early offensive outburst from reserve wing Jayden Ross that helped keep things close as UCLA got off to a hot start. The Huskies got point guard Silas Demary Jr. back from injury, and he was able to provide 22 minutes off the bench after missing the first-round win over Furman. Demary should be full strength for Friday’s battle of two coaches with impressive March track records when Dan Hurley’s Huskies take on Tom Izzo and Michigan State.Even without Josh Jefferson, the Cyclones clobbered Kentucky on Sunday. Their pressure controlled the game, forcing a staggering 20 turnovers and helping them win the second half by 18 points. Jefferson’s ankle injury is serious, though, and will likely keep him out of at least Iowa State’s Sweet 16 contest against Tennessee on Friday. Without him, Iowa State still possesses its outstanding defensive identity, but its potential would be limited against top competition — including Michigan, which might be the next team up with a Final Four berth on the line. No. 15 Tennessee State108-74Back-to-back 90-plus-point performances have John Calipari and the Hogs in the Sweet 16 for the second straight season. Arkansas needed every bit of another spectacular Darius Acuff performance (36 points, six assists) to knock out the tournament’s last remaining mid-major, a High Point team that pushed the favorites to the limit. The Hogs allowed High Point to shoot 65 percent inside the arc; that number is a neon warning sign ahead of a matchup with an enormous Arizona squad in San Jose.The Red Storm held Kansas to just 53 points through the first 35 minutes, but a late Jayhawks push tied the game with 13 seconds left. Then, an unlikely hero emerged: Dylan Darling, who tallied his first basket of the game as the buzzer sounded to send Rick Pitino and the Johnnies to the Sweet 16. A colossal clash with Duke awaits in Washington D.C., a game packed with storylines that will garner national attention.No. 12 Northern Iowa79-53Tom Izzo’s squad out-physicaled Louisville on Saturday, winning the rebounding battle on both ends and making more than double the free throws (14) that the Cardinals attempted (six). The Spartans led the entire contest, and the margin was relatively comfortable for the final five minutes. Most notable for MSU’s title aspirations: They are 21 of 46 (45.7 percent) from beyond the arc so far in the NCAA Tournament. The Spartans now take on Dan Hurley’s UConn Huskies on Friday in Washington D.C.No. 14 North Dakota State92-67A week ago, Nebraska had zero NCAA Tournament wins in school history. Now, the Cornhuskers are in the Sweet 16 after eviscerating Troy on Thursday and then winning a thriller against Vanderbilt on Saturday night. Braden Frager’s driving layup with 2.2 seconds left was the difference in the second round, as the Commodores’ 60-foot heave at the horn barely rimmed out. The Huskers got some help in their region, as well: Their path has opened up thanks to No. 9 seed Iowa knocking off No. 1 Florida on Sunday night. The Volunteers controlled most of the game against No. 3 seed Virginia on Sunday, and they held on late despite the Cavaliers making a run to take a brief lead with under two minutes to play. Head coach Rick Barnes now has Tennessee in the Sweet 16 for the fourth consecutive season, and he got this team there despite star freshman Nate Ament only mustering 16 total points across the Vols’ two weekend games. Tennessee’s chances of making a run increased with Joshua Jefferson’s ankle injury, as it slightly weakens No. 2 seed Iowa State ahead of the teams’ meeting in Chicago on Friday.No Aden Holloway, no problem. The Crimson Tide exploded for 19 3s against Texas Tech on Sunday night in an easy win. That shooting display was especially impressive without Holloway, who remained out after being arrested in Tuscaloosa on a drug charge before the tournament started. The Tide will need to repeat that offensive effort to counter the interior onslaught of top-seeded Michigan on Friday in Chicago.What an upset in Tampa! Alvaro Folgueiras’ go-ahead 3 with four seconds remaining stunned the South Region’s top seed, Florida, for what was easily Iowa’s most impressive win of the year. In his debut season, coach Ben McCollum has Iowa back in the Sweet 16 for the first time since 1999. The Hawkeyes now head south to Houston, where they will take on a familiar foe in Big Ten counterpart Nebraska. The two played twice in the final three weeks of the regular season, with Iowa winning at home and Nebraska winning in overtime in Lincoln. The Longhorns are the lone double-digit seed in the Sweet 16 and the first team that played in the First Four to advance to the second weekend since UCLA in 2021. The Longhorns have beaten NC State, BYU and Gonzaga, emerging as an exceedingly well-funded “Cinderella” in a tournament generally lacking in upsets. The shot making of Tramon Mark and Jordan Pope has been superb, and the frontcourt tandem of Dailyn Swain and Matas Vokietaitis has given opponents fits. This is a highly capable No. 11 seed.The Bracket Central series is sponsored by E*Trade from Morgan Stanley.The Athletic maintains full editorial independence.
